title: MCMC joint substitution+selector posterior estimation
hypothesis: a Bayesian MCMC/HMM estimator localises K4's plaintext where point-optimisation could not
best_partial: mean marginal posterior entropy 4.09/4.7 bits; 0/73 positions <1 bit; 0 distinct English in posterior
insights: MCMC (Metropolis-Hastings, beta=6.0, 6 chains, 4800 thinned samples) over the joint (free-position selector class x k=4 hand-crafted alphabets) posterior, cribs enforced via a fixed proper 3-colouring. Classical sampler, no LLM.

BAYESIAN UNDER-DETERMINATION: mean per-free-position marginal posterior entropy = 4.09 bits (max 4.70); only 0/73 free positions are near-determined (<1 bit). 0 distinct English-level decryptions appear in the posterior.

The posterior is DIFFUSE (mean marginal entropy 4.09 bits ~ near-uniform) -- the cribs + ciphertext do not localise the plaintext; the MCMC/HMM estimator CONFIRMS the under-determination (092/093/098) from a Bayesian angle, by a method (posterior sampling) distinct from the 093 optimisation and the 106 CP-SAT proof.
next_steps: MCMC confirms the diffuse posterior; the under-determination is now shown three ways (092 analytic, 093 optimisation, 106 CP-SAT, 107 Bayesian). A sharper plaintext prior (Sanborn-conditioned, exp 108) is the only remaining lever within decipherment-only
